sources.headline: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
sources.text: Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't. The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi, co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders?The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch. Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes, has called it "a dangerous escalation".It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism. Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga. Some of Ukraine's more audacious long-range drone attacks – what Zelensky likes to call "long-range sanctions" – have also struck targets thousands of kilometres beyond Ukraine's borders with Russia, deep inside Siberia. The most notable of these was last year's Operation Spider's Web, which involved a specially adapted lorry that drove close to a Russian strategic nuclear bomber airbase and released a "swarm" of explosive drones that damaged or destroyed several expensive bombers.And Ukraine has also been active further south in Africa where its forces have targeted Russian mercenaries from the Africa Corps, the successor to the infamous Wagner Group that was accused of carrying out numerous human rights abuses.It's not just Russia that will be alarmed by this latest Ukrainian operation in Benghazi harbour. The United Nations mission in Libya has already expressed its "deep concern". Libyan officials point out that their country is not a party to the Russia-Ukraine war, although the Merkury and an accompanying cargo ship that was also hit were berthed in the eastern part of Libya controlled by the pro-Moscow warlord and self-styled "Field Marshal" Khalifa Haftar.

From the show      
  Reading time 1 min 
 Talk about spillover. In the Libyan port of Benghazi, Ukraine claiming responsibility for the sinkings first of a Russian warship and then a cargo vessel. That’s on top of the sanctioned ship struck in the Baltic Sea that’s since strayed into Finland’s waters. Legitimate targets?  
 
With Russia taking out the frustration of a stalled ground invasion on civilian targets stalemate, what’s fair game for Ukraine to target? More broadly, why’s the naval war spreading from Europe's shores? Already it’s global food supplies affected by the suspected Russian targeting of civilian cargo ships in the Black Sea. We’ll ask how Africa’s affected by the attack on Benghazi, Benghazi a hub for Russia’s mercenary forces on the continent. The planet had mostly forgotten Libya’s own enduring stalemate, the one between rebel strongman Khalifa Haftar and the UN-backed government in Tripoli. Could two inconclusive conflicts become one?

sources.headline: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
sources.text:
In this image made from video provided by Russian Defense Ministry Press Service on Sunday, July 16, 2023, a Russian navy corvette Merkury attends naval military exercises in the Baltic Sea.
Russian Defense Ministry Press Service/AP
hide caption
Russian Defense Ministry Press Service/AP
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day. Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information "if deemed to be appropriate." The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army. At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings. A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said. Three people were killed Monday in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.
Also on Monday, the European Commission proposed a new round of sanctions to keep economic pressure on Moscow, targeting dozens of Russian banks, cracking down on crypto platforms and slapping bans on sports teams and athletes competing under the country's flag. The proposals, put forward by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, must be endorsed by all 27 European Union member countries before they can enter into force. The process can take weeks, and the planned measures are likely to be modified. The bloc has already hit more than 4,700 people and entities, including President Vladimir Putin, and several energy companies. Zelenskyy lauds Ukrainian attacks from Siberia to Libya Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved." "We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said. Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin. An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work Monday after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometers (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack. Russian officials also reported Monday a Ukrainian attack on industrial sites in Russia's Perm region, more than 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from Ukraine. One person was killed in the attack, and 56 Ukrainian drones were downed, Perm Gov. Dmitri Makhonin said. "We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said. Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that the forces also destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter that was on the Merkury.
Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials. The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital of Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential matters. Sunday's attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials, although Zelenskyy claimed it was sunk. Benghazi residents heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defense units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said. The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of an agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo. The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the U.N. Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch the attack. Libyan officials say 2 sea drones hit Russian warship Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told AP that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships. At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said. The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition aboard the Merkury. Hours after the warship attack, another sea drone strike hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel sailing off Benghazi, the Libyan coast guard said. The Russian cargo ship was sanctioned, Ukraine says Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, while the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara. The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a "mother ship" near the target, the SBU said. Russian defenses tried to intercept the attacking drones, it said. "Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes," the SBU said.

sources.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine sank Russian warship off Libya's coast
sources.text:
Updated on: November 23, 2026 / 8:20 PM EST
/ CBS/AP
Add CBS News on Google
Kyiv, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was behind an attack on a Russian warship off Libya on Sunday, claiming Ukrainian naval drones sank the vessel. It marked the latest attack in the North African nation tied to the Russia-Ukraine war. Zelenskyy said Monday in a social media post that Ukrainian forces deployed seven domestically made naval drones in the operation, which sank a Russian corvette. The Ukrainian leader described the ship as one of Russia's newest vessels commissioned in 2023 during Russia's invasion."Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk," he wrote. He added that a Ka-27 military helicopter was destroyed in the attack.
A satellite image shows a capsized Russian corvette and the northern area of the port after an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base, which Libya's eastern-based government said was caused by a suspected drone attack, in Benghazi, Libya, on Nov. 22, 2026. The vessel later sank, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
Vantor / Handout via REUTERS
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said. Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara off Libya on Sunday. Zelenskyy said Moscow had used the vessel to transport weapons. The Angara has been under U.S. and international sanctions for illegally transporting weapons for Russia. Another Russia-linked cargo ship, the Sparta II, which is operated by Russian defense logistics firm Oboronlogistika, was struck by drones Saturday in international waters in the Gulf of Finland, causing a fire on board. Kyiv has not confirmed or denied any role in that attack, but Finland's military said it was likely a Ukrainian strike. The Sparta is also under U.S. sanctions for illicit transportation of military hardware.Russian, Estonian and Finnish vessels helped put out the fire and all crew members were rescued from the Sparta, and a Russian ship then started towing it away Sunday, according to Reuters.
Zelenskyy thanked the Security Service of Ukraine, known as the SBU, and other Ukrainian defense forces that took part in the strikes off Libya's coast, which he called "an exemplary Ukrainian operation in response to Russia's war." Zelenskyy said he received detailed briefings on Sunday and Monday and that "the targets we set were achieved."The Kremlin made no immediate comment on the strikes off Libya, but said the Russian defense ministry would provide information later about the attacks. Referring to the strike in the Gulf of Finland, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters on Monday that it was "indeed a very dangerous trend — the expansion of terrorist activity in the Baltic region ... This is very dangerous. It is, of course, leading to an escalation of tensions in the region."
Russia "would like to hope that the Baltic states will somehow use their influence" on Ukraine to "warn it against continuing such dangerous terrorist practices," Peskov said.The operation off Libya's coast, conducted some 1,500 miles from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces. Ukraine has at times blindsided Russia during the war with ingenious attacks that embarrass Moscow, such as Operation Spider's Web in June last year, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft on bases across Russia. The latest strike by sea drones severely damaged the Russian navy corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials. Residents in Benghazi heard loud explosions and saw fire at the base early Sunday. Civil defense rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Qaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A U.N.-supported government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.The U.N. mission in Libya expressed "serious concern" over the latest attack and called for "an immediate, independent and transparent investigation."
"Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts," the United Nations Support Mission in Libya (UNSMIL) wrote on social media.Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West. They used the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials. The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were at the time operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year. The SBU described the latest operation as "unique." It said the drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a so-called "mothership" near the target. Russian defenses tried from air, sea and land to hit the attacking drones, it said. "Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes, even far beyond the Black Sea," which borders both Russia and Ukraine, the SBU said.Russia hammered Ukrainian cities with another deadly round of airstrikes overnight, meanwhile.Regional authorities said 17 people were killed as a result of Russian attacks on Kyiv and the southern Zaporizhzhia region, including one child. Dozens more have been injured.

Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack

No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia

Dan Sabbagh in Kharkiv and Angelique Chrisafis
Sun 22 Nov 2026 16.33 EST
Share
Prefer the Guardian on Google

A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.

The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press.

View image in fullscreen
Aerial view of the Russian naval vessel Merkury before it was struck in the port of Benghazi, Libya, 21 November 2026. Photograph: 2026 Vantor/EPA

Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine, marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war.

Though Ukraine began the war with no navy, it has developed a sea drone capability that threatened Russian warships in the Black Sea. The Russian fleet has been forced to retreat to the eastern port of Novorossiysk because Sevastopol in occupied Crimea had become unsafe.

Hours later, a Russia-linked cargo ship said to be carrying military supplies, the Ascalon, was hit by a sea drone off the coast of Benghazi. Video showed the drone heading directly towards one end of the vessel, again causing a huge explosion.

Libyan naval forces ‌rescued the vessel’s crew, the ‌sources added. The health ministry said some crew members were in stable condition with minor injuries. The number of injured and their nationalities are not known.

Benghazi is controlled by the self-styled Libyan National Army, led by Gen Khalifa Haftar, which controls eastern and southern Libya and has been aligned with Russia.

There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range attacks against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

The UN mission in Libya (Unsmil) expressed “serious concern” over the two drone attacks off Benghazi and called for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation”, in a post on X.

The ‌eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that ​normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.

It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and ⁠a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take ​legal and ​diplomatic measures against ​anyone found responsible.

“The Libyan government will not ​allow Libyan ‌ports, territory or territorial ​waters ​to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

0:55
Large blaze at Benghazi port after suspected drone attack on Russian warship – video

The specialist website Naval News earlier identified the ship attacked as the Merkury, a Russian corvette – the smallest class of warship, smaller than a frigate – and said it had almost certainly been destroyed.

HI Sutton, a naval analyst, said the attack was probably conducted by sea drones, after a photograph of one emerged apparently taken off the Libyan coast. The drone, he said, “is also likely the type used in the subsequent attack”. Similar-looking drones were involved in the subsequent attack on the Ascalon cargo ship.

View image in fullscreen
An explosion on the ship in Benghazi, where it had been refuelling on its way back to Russia. Photograph: X.com

If it is confirmed that Ukraine has been able to blow up or seriously damage a Russian warship in Benghazi, it would represent one of its most successful naval strikes during the almost five-year war.

But it also represents a risky extension of the fighting far beyond eastern Europe, in an incident that could affect civilians on another continent and the working of the port.

A small unit of Ukrainian special forces operatives has been based at Misrata, western Libya, and is believed to have coordinated drone attacks on Russian tankers and transport ships in the past year.

Russian ships regularly make use of the port, which has a growing military importance to the Kremlin, to supply Russian mercenary forces in Africa and as a base in the Mediterranean since the country lost its bases in Syria.

Separately, a fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was ⁠struck by drones in the ⁠Baltic Sea continued to smoulder ​on Sunday, Finland’s border guard said, with emergency services from Finland, Russia and Estonia working together to put out the blaze.

View image in fullscreen
Emergency services working to extinguish a fire onboard the Russian cargo ship Sparta II, which was struck in the Baltic Sea on Saturday. Photograph: Finnish Border Guard/Reuters

The Finnish military said the strike on the Sparta II ⁠on Saturday was probably carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters, where it remained at anchor. The 16 crew members were evacuated on to a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly ⁠injured.

On Sunday, visible flames had been put out, with operations focusing on cooling down the containers and stabilising the vessel, Finnish authorities said.

The ship, bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, had been damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, Finland’s defence forces said, corroborating an account by Russian officials. Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia’s north-west coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling on to Nato territory.

The risk of ⁠further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, could not be ruled ​out, Ivo Värk, the Estonian navy commander, told the public ​broadcaster ERR on Sunday.

Finland’s military said last ​week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.

Suspected drone strike hits Russian ship at Libya’s Benghazi port, raising regional security concerns

By Nela Heidner
Published on 22 November 2026 - 18:11 GMT+1
A suspected drone strike on a Russian ship at Libya’s Benghazi port has raised concerns over the spread of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Authorities are investigating the blast amid growing fears for regional security.

A powerful explosion aboard a Russian vessel docked at Libya’s eastern port of Benghazi has raised concerns that the Russia-Ukraine war could be extending into North Africa, after local authorities suggested the ship may have been targeted in a drone attack.

Officials from Libya’s eastern administration said the explosion occurred on Sunday while the Russian ship was stationed at the port for refuelling and resupply before returning to Russia.

No casualties were reported, although the incident prompted an emergency response and heightened security concerns around the port.

In an official statement, the eastern authorities indicated that drones were suspected of striking the vessel. No group or government immediately claimed responsibility.

The administration also emphasised that Libya was not involved in the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, seeking to distance the country from any suggestion that its territory was being used as a battleground in the ongoing war.

Conflicting initial reports and investigation

Early accounts of the explosion suggested that a fire had erupted at an ammunition storage facility within a naval installation in Benghazi. However, Libya’s eastern authorities subsequently clarified that the blast originated aboard a Russian ship docked at the port.

Local television reports described emergency crews being dispatched to the affected area to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading to nearby facilities.

Al-Masar television, citing civil defence personnel, reported that firefighters had been deployed to a military facility following the explosion. Libya Alhadath television also reported that residents were advised to avoid the surrounding area while emergency operations were underway. The fire was later brought under control.

Although Libyan authorities did not identify the vessel or disclose details of its cargo, naval analysts have provisionally identified it as the Russian missile corvette Merkury, which is believed to have sustained extensive damage in the explosion.

Libya’s eastern-based government announced plans to conduct a joint investigation with Russian officials to establish the circumstances surrounding the explosion.

Suspected attack comes amid expanding conflict

The Benghazi incident comes against the backdrop of increasingly extensive Ukrainian operations targeting Russian military infrastructure, energy facilities and maritime assets beyond the conventional battlefield.

According to the supplied reports, a Russian cargo vessel was struck by a drone in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, near Finnish waters. Finland’s military said Ukraine was likely responsible for the attack, although Kyiv has not claimed responsibility.

Although no evidence has been publicly presented linking Ukraine to the Benghazi explosion, the timing has drawn attention to the growing geographical reach of attacks associated with the war.

Russia has previously accused Ukraine of targeting vessels involved in transporting Russian energy exports, including ships operating far from the Black Sea.

The latest developments have raised questions about the vulnerability of commercial shipping routes, port facilities and maritime logistics networks in regions traditionally considered outside the immediate conflict zone.

Libya warns against becoming a battleground for foreign powers

The suspected strike has also exposed the security challenges facing Libya, where competing political authorities continue to exercise control over different parts of the country.

The internationally recognised Government of National Unity, based in Tripoli, expressed concern about the possibility of civilian maritime infrastructure being drawn into foreign military operations.

In a statement, the Tripoli administration warned against using Libyan ports and other civilian facilities for activities connected to international conflicts.

It stressed that Libya should not become a staging ground for foreign military confrontations or logistical operations that could threaten national security and sovereignty.

The statement reflects broader concerns that Libya’s strategic Mediterranean location, combined with its prolonged political fragmentation, could expose the country to escalating geopolitical tensions.

Previous maritime incidents heighten concerns

The Benghazi explosion follows other reported incidents involving Russian vessels in and around the Mediterranean.

In March, a Russian liquefied natural gas carrier was severely damaged off the Libyan coast following an attack. Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed Ukraine for the incident, although responsibility remained a matter of dispute.

The vessel was reportedly associated with Russia’s so-called shadow fleet, a network of ships used to transport Russian energy exports while navigating Western sanctions and restrictions.

Ukraine has previously acknowledged operations against vessels linked to Russian maritime trade, including an attack in the Mediterranean in December of the previous year.

Such incidents have intensified concerns over the potential consequences of maritime attacks, particularly near civilian ports and international shipping corridors.

Apart from the immediate threat to vessels and crews, explosions involving ships can pose risks to port workers, coastal communities, commercial operations and the marine environment.

Russia’s presence in Libya adds strategic significance

Russia has maintained longstanding military and political relationships with influential actors in eastern Libya, including forces associated with military commander Khalifa Haftar.

Libya’s geographical position makes it strategically important for access to the Mediterranean, North Africa and the wider Sahel region.

The country has remained politically divided since the 2011 uprising that overthrew longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi. The internationally recognised administration in Tripoli, headed by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah, continues to face a rival eastern political and military establishment supported by Haftar.

This fragmentation has complicated efforts to establish unified national security institutions and limit foreign military involvement.

Investigation could determine wider implications

For now, significant questions remain unanswered, including whether the explosion was caused by a deliberate drone strike, who may have carried it out and whether the vessel was transporting military equipment.

sources.text: CAIRO – A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship on Nov 22 at a Libyan naval base, Libyan officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian Navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.They said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not allowed to talk to reporters.Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based in Tripoli and a rival administration in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Nov 22 caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.The Almasar satellite television channel aired footage showing a vessel erupting into flames. It said the Libyan navy rescued the crew of the Maltese-flagged ship. A corvette warship is smaller than a frigate or destroyer and is built to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.The vessel had docked at the base for refuelling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the east-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. There was no immediate comment from either Russia or Ukraine.A European official said the reports of an explosion at Benghazi Port involving a Russian vessel appeared to be credible.The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak on the record, said the vessel has been identified as a Russian corvette, adding they had no assessment of cause at this time.On the evening of Nov 22, local media said that another sea drone hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack. No further details were given. Almasar said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.The western Libya government expressed concerns about “dragging Libyan ports and civilian facilities into external conflicts,” in an apparent reference to Russia’s war in Ukraine.“The government reaffirms its categorical rejection of turning Libya into an arena for international conflicts or a theatre for external powers to settle scores,” it said in a statement.In March, Ukrainian forces operating in western Libya under a covert deal struck a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in a suspected sea drone attack near Maltese waters, Libyan officials said at the time.The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, operated mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also at other military facilities in the capital, Tripoli, and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press.
